name: Troeven
description: Troeven is a Dutch/Flemish trick-taking game where players start at a score (e.g., 7) and work down to zero. Uses a 32-card deck (7-A). The trump caller picks trump from first 4-5 cards. Win more card-value points (A=4, K=3, Q=2, J=1) than opponents to reduce score by 1. If trump caller loses, their team gains a point (penalty).

history.origins: Troeven is the Dutch name for this trick-taking game, popular in the southern Dutch province of Limburg. It was described by Harry Tiggelovend in The Playing-Card (volume XXIV, No 6). The name means trumps. The game is part of the Couillon family played in Belgium and the Netherlands and is likely related to the old Trumpfspiel recorded in Strasbourg in 1637, which had the same card values.
timeline: 20th century: Described by Harry Tiggelovend in The Playing-Card (volume XXIV, No 6); popular in the southern Dutch province of Limburg. Name means trumps.

setup.deck: 32 cards. A(high)-7(low). Values: A=4, K=3, Q=2, J=1. Total 40 pts.
setup.dealing: 8 cards each. Trump caller sees first 4-5 and declares.

rules.objective: Be the first team to cancel all seven branches (reduce your score from 7 to 0) by winning more card points than the opponents in each hand; the team that called trumps and loses adds a branch.
rules.gameplay: Trump caller declares trump. Play 8 tricks. Follow suit. Total 40 card points. Higher scorer reduces score by 1. Tie = no change. Trump caller losing = adds 1 (penalty).

strategy.basic: Call trump with Aces and Kings.
strategy.intermediate: Manage trump caller risk (penalty for losing).
